Parametric bootstrap likelihood ratio test of nested models

Source: R/pglmm-tests.R
pglmm_boot_LRT.Rd

Compares two nested models fitted by pglmm() (or pglmm_compare()) with a parametric bootstrap of their likelihood ratio, as pbkrtest::PBmodcomp() does for lme4 models: nsim responses are simulated from the smaller model (with new values of its random effects, see simulate.communityPGLMM() with re.form = NA), both models are refitted to each of them, and the p-value is the proportion of the simulated likelihood ratio statistics that are at least as large as the observed one, \((1 + \#\{LR_{sim} \ge LR_{obs}\}) / (n_{sim} + 1)\).

Usage

pglmm_boot_LRT(full, reduced, nsim = 500, seed = NULL, ncores = 1)

Arguments

full, reduced

Two nested models (in either order), fitted by pglmm() or pglmm_compare() to the same data.

nsim

Number of simulated data sets.

seed

Optional seed of the random number generator, for reproducible p-values.

ncores

Number of cores to refit the models with (parallel::mclapply(); one on Windows).

Value

An object of class pglmm_boot_LRT, a list with the observed likelihood ratio statistic (stat), its degrees of freedom (df), the p-values of the chi-square test (p.chisq) and of the bootstrap (p.boot), the simulated statistics (stat.sim), and the number of simulated data sets for which a model could not be fitted (n.failed, left out of the p-value).

Details

The chi-square test of anova() relies on the asymptotic distribution of the likelihood ratio, which can be far from it with few levels of the random terms or, in phylogenetic models, few effectively independent species. In simulations of binary data with phylogenetic signal (100 species, 15 sites), the Wald test of a fixed effect rejected a true null hypothesis in 8.6% to 9.8% of data sets and the chi-square likelihood ratio test in 10.6% to 11.2% (500 data sets), instead of 5%; the bootstrap test (199 simulations) rejected it in 4% of 100 data sets. It also gives a valid test of a variance at the boundary (zero), where the chi-square test is conservative.

As with anova(), models fitted with REML = TRUE that differ in their fixed effects are refitted by maximum likelihood first. The models must have been fitted with bayes = FALSE (and binomial and poisson models with method = "Laplace") to the same data, and from a call that can be evaluated again (their data in the environment of their formula, as for update()). Simulations ignore the prior weights of poisson, negative binomial and Gamma models (as simulate.communityPGLMM()).

See also

anova.communityPGLMM(), pglmm_profile_LRT()

Examples

# \donttest{
# a test of a fixed effect with binary data (few simulations, for speed)
set.seed(1)
phy <- ape::rcoal(30)
d <- expand.grid(sp = phy$tip.label, site = paste0("s", 1:6), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d$x <- rnorm(nrow(d))
d$pa <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, 0.4)
m1 <- pglmm(pa ~ x + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site), data = d, family = "binomial",
            cov_ranef = list(sp = phy), REML = FALSE)
#> boundary (singular) fit: the variances of 1|sp__, 1|site are (close to) zero; see ?pglmm_is_singular
m0 <- pglmm(pa ~ 1 + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site), data = d, family = "binomial",
            cov_ranef = list(sp = phy), REML = FALSE)
#> boundary (singular) fit: the variances of 1|sp__, 1|site are (close to) zero; see ?pglmm_is_singular
pglmm_boot_LRT(m1, m0, nsim = 50, seed = 2)
#> Parametric bootstrap likelihood ratio test
#>   reduced: pa ~ 1 + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site) 
#>   full:    pa ~ x + (1 | sp__) + (1 | site) 
#> 
#>              stat df p.value
#> Chi-square 0.4519  1  0.5015
#> Bootstrap  0.4519 NA  0.4314
#> 
#> 50 simulated data sets
# }
